brief: GS TMT Spec Sales morning note (8 Oct 2026). Overnight tape rotated: semis/software lagged while memory, AI hardware and beaten-up internet names outperformed, with firm memory pricing and supply constraints (including a threatened Micron Taiwan strike) supporting the memory outlook. Samsung posted a fourth straight record quarter but slightly missed street and shares slipped as investors debated the result; TSMC beat guidance on AI-chip demand. Samsung is reportedly advancing HBM4E qualification with Nvidia/hyperscalers though production size is undecided, while downstream OEMs (LG Innotek) face margin pressure from rising memory costs. AI capex financing is expanding: Broadcom is exploring ~$30bn of debt financing for OpenAI's custom chips, following its $60bn Anthropic deal, with Oracle and SpaceX seeking similar financing; Terafab and ASML's setup stay open questions, with hedge funds reportedly using ASML as a sector funding short. Prime brokerage data shows clients rotating back into Mag7 and semis (near multi-year exposure highs) even as overall net positioning stays low. The note also carries a grab-bag of single-name items: a bearish DSY stance, a bullish Capgemini view, a VOD UK guidance raise, Prosus/JET's growth inflection, SpaceX's FCC Starlink approval, a CityFibre going-concern warning, and a Telefónica contract win.
